newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real fell 0.21 pct on dollar outflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real fell 0.21 pct on dollar outflows.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.21 percent to close at 1.0206 against the greenback on dollar outflows in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Thursday deficit of $120 million.
The deficit was expected due to payments on maturing Eurobonds, but some other transactions also led to larger-than-expected dollar outflows, dealers said.
"Everybody was anticipating more dollar outflows, but we were not expecting so much," one trader said.
Dealers said the market was likely to open nervous on Friday, with some speculating the Central Bank would lower the real-dollar mini-band, currently between 1.018 and 1.023 reais to the dollar.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0237 to the dollar, down 0.07 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 0.39 percent to end at 1.034 per greenback due to a reduction in the supply of dollars, traders said.
